units.source: Manually altering the database
units.context: Manually altering the database

units.source: There are some situations where modifying the SQLite database that Trilium uses is desirable.
units.context: Manually altering the database

units.source: If you are doing any advanced development or troubleshooting where you manually modify the database, you might want to consider creating backups of your __TRILIUM_PH_0__ file.
units.context: Manually altering the database

units.source: Modifying it internally using the SQL Console__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Manually altering the database > Modifying it internally using the SQL Console

units.source: The SQL Console is Trilium's built-in database editor.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Modifying it internally using the SQL Console

units.source: See __TRILIUM_PH_0__SQL Console__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Modifying it internally using the SQL Console

units.source: Externally modifying the database__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database

units.source: Sometimes the SQL Console cannot be used (for example if the application cannot start).
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database

units.source: When making external modifications, consider closing the desktop application. If modifying the server database, then stop the service or Docker container.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database

units.source: Using DB Browser for SQLite__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using DB Browser for SQLite

units.source: DB Browser for SQLite is a cross-platform editor that can be used to alter the database using a graphical user interface.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using DB Browser for SQLite

units.source: To do so:
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using DB Browser for SQLite

units.source: In the main menu, select File → Open database… and navigate to the database in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Data directory__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using DB Browser for SQLite

units.source: Select the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Execute SQL__TRILIUM_PH_1__ tab.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using DB Browser for SQLite

units.source: Type in the desired SQL statement.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using DB Browser for SQLite

units.source: Press the "Play" button in the toolbar underneath the "Execute SQL" tab (or F5 key).
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using DB Browser for SQLite

units.source: Press "Write Changes" in the main toolbar.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using DB Browser for SQLite

units.source: Close the application or close the database.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using DB Browser for SQLite

units.source: Using the SQLite CLI__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using the SQLite CLI

units.source: First, start the SQLite 3 CLI by specifying the path to the database:
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using the SQLite CLI

units.source: In the prompt simply type the statement and make sure it ends with a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ character.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using the SQLite CLI

units.source: To exit, simply type __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and enter.
units.context: Manually altering the database > Externally modifying the database > Using the SQLite CLI
